Proven background knowledge or initiated experience in electronic circuit and hardware development, including digital/analog electronics, schematic capture, hardware integration, and hands-on testing and troubleshooting of circuit card assemblies.
Proven background knowledge or initiated experience in Radio Frequency (RF) testing, schematic capture, circuit design, and hardware selection and integration.

posting.title: PhD Autonomy Engineer Intern - Deep Learning / Computer Vision, 2027
posting.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

About the role:

The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry.

As a PhD Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products.

If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development with relevant research and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you.

How you'll make an impact:

 - Enable rapid research and development of intelligent systems with advanced autonomous capabilities beyond anything that exists in the world today

 - Research, prototype, and generally assess the feasibility of new approaches

 - Imagine and then implement new features that unlock magic for our users

 - Characterize and quantify the performance of core components of the software and hardware stack

What makes you a strong fit:

 - High proficiency in C++ and/or Python

 - Demonstrated enthusiasm for one or more of the following: computer vision, deep learning, motion planning, dynamics and controls, 3D graphics, embedded software/firmware, distributed systems, tools/infrastructure, mobile

 - Solid software engineering foundation and a commitment to writing clean, well-architected code

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative, small team environment

Compensation Range: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Masters, and $70/hr for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends.

*For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual's regional location.

#LI-DK1

We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture.

Prepare summaries, updates, and presentation materials for team and leadership reviews.
You will have exposure to several areas of product development, sourcing, operations, and productivity at Stanley Black & Decker. Be a rising junior or senior with a target graduation date of 2026 or 2027.

Maintains strong academic credentials.
Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to work effectively across cross-functional teams.
Interest in product development, sourcing, manufacturing, value engineering, productivity, or cost optimization.

Successfully manages strong academics alongside extracurricular activities.

This position will provide you with:
A utility role interacting with key members of a Fortune 500 company.
A flexible schedule featuring a max of 40 hours.
Opportunity for career advancement upon graduation.
Competitive compensation and career development opportunities.

posting.title: Construction and Architecture Intern
posting.description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Construction and Architecture Intern, you’ll get hands-on experience bringing a factory to life - designing and standing up the processes that make our products real. You’ll work alongside engineers, operators, and builders in a fast-paced, highly collaborative environment, contributing to everything from facility layouts to construction progress tracking. This is a chance to learn by doing, where your work will directly shape how we deliver affordable energy at scale.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Support coordination between civil engineering team and manufacturing team to align facility design with production requirements.

 - Assist with reviewing interior build-out plans, MEP layouts, warehouse racking, and equipment move-in logistics to ensure efficient setup and compliance with requirements.

 - Participate in design and construction meetings, capturing action items and tracking progress on civil-related deliverables.

 - Contribute to quantity takeoffs, cost tracking, and documentation for civil works tied to the factory build.

 - Conduct field visits to observe construction activities, verify work against plans, and report findings to the project team.
   


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Strong organizational skills and ability to manage details across multiple stakeholders.

 - Interest in facility design, construction methods, and how they intersect with manufacturing operations.

 - Ability to read or interpret construction drawings, layouts, and technical documentation.

 - Eagerness to participate in fieldwork, site walks, and hands-on problem solving.

 - Analytical mindset for tracking costs, quantities, and progress against plans.

 - Clear communication skills for documenting action items and sharing findings with cross-functional teams.

 - Proactive, “learn by doing” attitude with willingness to dive into new technical areas.



About the Team

The Infrastructure & Development team builds and maintains the physical foundation that enables Base Power to operate and grow. We own the full lifecycle of capital projects—factory builds, manufacturing line installations, and headquarters—acting as the primary stewards of our physical footprint. We move fast, make decisions with confidence, and hold our design and construction partners to a high standard. Every project we deliver creates the physical conditions for Base Power to scale.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

posting.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.

The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry.

As an Autonomy Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products.

If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development with relevant research and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you.

How you'll make an impact:

 - Enable rapid research and development of intelligent systems with advanced autonomous capabilities beyond anything that exists in the world today

 - Research, prototype, and generally assess the feasibility of new approaches

 - Imagine and then implement new features that unlock magic for our users

 - Characterize and quantify the performance of core components of the software and hardware stack

What makes you a strong fit:

 - High proficiency in C++ and/or Python

 - Demonstrated enthusiasm for one or more of the following: computer vision, deep learning, motion planning, dynamics and controls, 3D graphics, embedded software/firmware, distributed systems, tools/infrastructure, mobile

 - Solid software engineering foundation and a commitment to writing clean, well-architected code

 - Ability to thrive in a fast-paced, collaborative, small team environment

posting.title: 2027 Summer Intern, Onboard Autonomy, Embodied AI (Masters)
posting.description:
Job Description
Work Arrangement:
Hybrid: This internship is categorized as on-site. The selected intern is expected to report to the office 3 days a week.
Location:
Sunnyvale, CA
Seattle, WA
About the Team
The Onboard Autonomy team develops the real-time intelligence that enables autonomous vehicles to perceive their surroundings, plan safe and comfortable behavior, and operate reliably on the vehicle. Our work spans sensor fusion, structured perception, trajectory generation, ML planning, local planning, controls, guardrails, evaluation, and vehicle integration.
We combine machine learning, robotics, optimization, and software engineering to build production-oriented autonomy systems that operate in real time and handle challenging driving scenarios.
About the Role
As an Onboard Autonomy Intern, you will contribute to a focused research or engineering project within the onboard driving stack. You will work with experienced researchers and engineers to prototype, evaluate, and improve algorithms or software using vehicle data, simulation, or production-oriented environments.
Potential focus areas include:
Sensor Encoders and Fusion: Convert camera, lidar, radar, and other sensor inputs into useful representations for autonomy.
Structured Perception: Improve object tracking, online maps, scene understanding, and long-tail scenario handling.
ML Planning and Trajectory Generation: Predict behavior, generate trajectories, and select safe driving actions.
Local Planning and Controls: Balance collision avoidance, traffic rules, vehicle dynamics, kinematic feasibility, and passenger comfort.
Guardrails and Integration: Validate and integrate autonomy components across vehicle platforms to support safe, reliable operation.
What You’ll Do
Prototype and evaluate algorithms for perception, prediction, planning, trajectory generation, controls, or integration.
Work with real-world driving data and simulation to measure performance and investigate failures.
Build data-processing, visualization, testing, and evaluation tools.
Contribute to production-quality software through design reviews, code reviews, automated testing, continuous integration, and documentation.
Analyze results, improve system performance, collaborate across disciplines, and present technical findings.
Required Qualifications
Currently pursuing a Master’s in Computer Science, Robotics, Electrical or Mechanical Engineering, Controls, Machine Learning, or a related STEM field.
Experience through coursework, research, projects, or professional work in machine learning, computer vision, robotics, controls, optimization, or autonomous systems.
Strong Python skills and experience with C++ or another systems programming language.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and collaboration skills.
Availability to work full-time, 40 hours per week, during the internship.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with autonomous vehicles, ADAS, robotics, or ROS.
Experience with PyTorch, TensorFlow, JAX, deep learning, transformers, multimodal learning, reinforcement learning, imitation learning, or trajectory prediction.
Background in vehicle dynamics, feedback control, trajectory optimization, motion planning, safety-critical software, simulation, closed-loop evaluation, sensor data, large-scale datasets, or distributed computing.
Intent to return to a degree program after the internship or co-op.
Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2028
Compensation:
The monthly salary range for this role is $11,800 per month
GM will provide a one-time lump sum taxable stipend payment to eligible students selected for the 2027 Student Program.

Paid U.S. GM holidays.
GM Family First Vehicle Discount Program.

Mentorship and hands-on experience with the data and ML foundations behind autonomy

Our vision is a world with Zero Crashes, Zero Emissions and Zero Congestion and we embrace the responsibility to lead the change that will make our world better, safer and more equitable for all.
Why Join Us
We believe we all must make a choice every day – individually and collectively – to drive meaningful change through our words, our deeds and our culture. Every day, we want every employee to feel they belong to one General Motors team.

posting.title: Engineering & Technology Innovation, Graduate Researcher Program – Advanced Materials & Structures Intern
posting.description:
Engineering & Technology Innovation, Graduate Researcher Program – Advanced Materials & Structures Intern
Company:
At Boeing, we are all innovators on a mission to connect, protect, explore and inspire. From the seabed to outer space, you’ll learn and grow, contributing to work that shapes the world. Find your future with us.
Join our exclusive
Graduate Researcher Program (GRP)
in Engineering & Technology Innovation (E&TI) during the Summer of 2027 and you can build something better for yourself, for our customers and for the world.  E&TI is Boeing's global research and development team developing and implementing innovative technologies that make the impossible possible and enabling the future of aerospace. We are engineers and technicians, skilled scientists and bold innovators. Join us and put your passion, determination, and skill to work building the future! #TheFutureIsBuiltHere #ChangeTheWorld
What is Graduate Researcher Program?
The GRP (Graduate Researcher Program) is a unique 10-12 week internship program designed specifically for students pursuing their PhD. GRP is a hybrid experience of real-world industry work experience combined with development programming that exposes students to Boeing, its products, services and its people.  GRP focuses on deeply connecting students to their team and Boeing through work experience across multiple summers with the goal of ultimately offering a full-time position at the conclusion of academic studies if a mutual fit is achieved.
How GRP Works
:
GRP host teams post intern requisitions aligned with Boeing’s strategic needs, aiming to match needs with top PhD talent. Once candidates apply and are selected, they receive an offer to spend the following summer working with their host team. The program is designed to give interns meaningful, hands-on experience at Boeing, allowing them to apply their academic expertise while contributing to real-world industry challenges and opportunities.
In addition to industry work exposure, students attend GRP programming to further broaden their experience and knowledge of Boeing.  GRP programming components include:  mentorship in your field of study, weekly
Featured Speaker Talks
, a week-long in-person
GRP Summit
, participation in an
Innovation Challenge
, and other opportunities to interact and build a professional network with other GRP students, Boeing team members, and Boeing leadership.
Please note:  The work you do at Boeing can be
related
to your area of study, but
cannot
contribute or be used in your PhD thesis.
Who we are looking for
:
We are seeking students who will have
completed their
first year of study
in their PhD program by July 2027 and are passionate about the aerospace industry and Boeing. GRP students excel at quickly adapting to their roles, analyzing complex problems, and developing innovative solutions. They thrive in collaborative team environments and possess excellent communication skills. Above all, they are driven to contribute to the success of their team, fellow GRP students, and Boeing.
2027 GRP Position
:
This position is with the Composite Materials & Structures team located in St. Louis, MO.  This team is at the forefront of developing advanced materials and manufacturing technologies that drive aerospace advancements in composite materials and structures.. The group develops, integrates, and transitions advanced structural architectures and design concepts. They also advance the state-of-the-art in methods and tools for structural analysis. They work across Boeing's product life-cycle and develop technologies for commercial aircraft, military aircraft, rotorcraft, space vehicles, UAVs, and advanced vehicle prototypes.
We are seeking a highly motivated PhD-level intern to join the Composite Material & Structures team. The GRP intern will support research and development efforts focused on composite materials, processing techniques, and manufacturing methodologies critical to next-generation aerospace structures.
Key Responsibilities will include:
Supporting development and documentation of engineering requirements, specifications, and process controls for composite materials and structures
Assisting in experimental research involving characterization, processing, and testing of advanced composite materials
Contributing to the evaluation and integration of emerging manufacturing technologies including automation and additive manufacturing for composite applications
Participating in failure analysis activities and helping to define corrective and preventative actions for composite materials and processes
Collaborating with cross-functional teams including manufacturing, design, supply chain, and suppliers to optimize composite materials and processes
Supporting supplier qualification efforts, including testing and audits related to composite material properties and processing
Documenting experimental data, preparing technical reports, and assisting with presentations on composite materials research outcomes
An internship with the Composite Materials & Structures group offers a unique opportunity to contribute to cutting-edge composite material research at Boeing’s ET&I organization.  The successful candidate will gain hands-on experience with innovative aerospace manufacturing and materials testing.
This position is expected to be 100% onsite.  The selected candidate will be required to work onsite at one of the listed location options.
This position
requires the ability to obtain U.S. Security Clearance for which the U.S. Government requires U.S. Citizenship.
Job Related Information / Basic Qualifications:
Completed the first year of PhD studies by July 2027
Ability to work full-time for 10-12 weeks during Summer 2027
Pursing a PhD in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Physics, or a related field with focus on composite materials & structures
Knowledge and/or hands-on experience with composite materials, which can include course work, experimental, or analytical training
Familiarity with materials failure mechanisms and testing standards for composites
Ability to analyze data using software tools like MATLAB, Python, or similar
Strong communication skills with ability to document and present technical findings
Preferred Qualifications:
Previous research or internship experience related to aerospace composite structures design, fabrication, analysis, and testing
Exposure to advanced manufacturing technologies such as automated fiber placement, additive manufacturing, or robotic processing
Interest in these areas: adhesive bonding, high temperature composites, performing material processing simulations, performing material qualification testing
Experience using CAD software, finite element analysis, or materials simulation tools is a plus

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

posting.title: 2027 Reliability Engineer Intern
posting.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
The Reliability Engineering team collaborates with our broader Engineering organization to ensure our products meet or exceed mission performance requirements, withstand challenging environmental conditions, and satisfy all customer specifications. As a Reliability Engineering Intern at Anduril, you will gain knowledge of advanced Reliability tools and methodologies to drive excellence into our products. You will support the Systems, Hardware, & Software Engineering teams across the product development lifecycle by participating in Failure Modes & Effects Analysis, predictive analysis, qualification test planning, field performance monitoring, and root cause & corrective action activities. The right person for this role enjoys hands-on work, loves to build processes, and can work efficiently across multi-disciplinary teams.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
Support review of system block diagrams, interface control documents, and schematics for compliance, redundancy, and accuracy against requirements.
Proactively identify product risks and drive root cause analysis & corrective actions.
Support Failure Modes & Effects Analysis activities and collaborate with other Engineering teams to implement product improvements for Reliability.
Support predictive reliability analysis efforts to calculate failure rates and Mean Time Between Failure metrics, utilizing Anduril requirements, specifications, and MIL-HDBK-217 Plus.
Support the development of Maintainability prediction models using MIL-HDBK-472.
Develop R&D and Qualification Test plans to ensure appropriate requirements coverage.
Work with Quality and Manufacturing Engineering to ensure inspection and acceptance test gates are in place and documented against requirements.
Perform Weibull analysis utilizing data from Qualification campaigns and from fielded assets.
Use data analysis techniques to highlight key problem areas for deployed products, propose corrective actions, and drive to closure.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related field.
Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester.
Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program.
Ability to complete a 12-week in-person internship in one of our offices in summer 2027.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Prior internship experience and/or leadership on a collegiate project team or laboratory.
Demonstrated hands-on fabrication skills.
Exposure to test plan development, test data acquisition, data analysis, and failure analysis techniques
Exposure to reliability analysis techniques, such as FMEA/FMECA, predictive modeling, Weibull analysis, and Fault Tree Analysis
Technical writing experience developing standards, specifications, user guides, and policies
Collegiate project team, machine shop, or laboratory experience.
High competence with, and fluid use of, engineering first principles.
Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to collaborate cross-functionally
Proficiency with the Microsoft Office Suite of tools

About Varda
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

Summer internships will range between the months of May and August. All dates
dependent upon the university schedule of the selected students. Internships are full-time and on-site in Los Angeles, CA. To be considered for this internship, candidates must be actively enrolled in an accredited undergraduate or graduate degree program.

This includes thrusters for primary maneuvers and attitude control, propellant tanks, and all associated plumbing and fluid components on the spacecraft. This system is completely designed, analyzed, fabricated, and tested in house which enables successful candidates exposure across all aspects of the design and manufacturing lifecycle of a space vehicle system.
Internships at Varda are optimal for students looking to grow technically and professionally while working on impactful projects critical to the company’s success. Job Description
About the Job
Join General Motors Research & Development as a Summer Research Intern supporting the Vehicle Defense Research group within the Safety, Engineering and Defense Research Lab. In this role, you will contribute to applied research, modeling and simulation, and technology development related to defense and military systems.
You will work with experienced researchers and engineers to evaluate current and emerging technologies, apply evidence-based analysis, and help translate research concepts into vehicle, system, and software applications for federal and defense customers.
This internship is designed for a graduate student who is interested in defense research, vehicle systems, modeling and simulation, autonomous systems, human-machine interaction, advanced powertrain and electrification, or related engineering disciplines.
The Role
As a Summer Research Intern, you will support research planning and execution across defense-focused modeling and simulation activities. You will collaborate with GM researchers, engineers, and external partners to conduct technical analyses, develop models or simulations, document results, and communicate findings.
You may contribute to projects involving:
Vehicle performance and mobility
Force-on-force and mission-level simulation
Autonomous systems
Human-machine interaction and user experience
Crew-compartment and Soldier-system simulation
Advanced powertrain, electrification, and power systems
Vehicle safety, testing, experimentation, and assessment
The specific project assignment will depend on business needs, your academic background, and your technical interests.
What You’ll Do:
Support research projects by defining objectives, conducting technical analysis, and documenting methods and results.
Develop, update, or apply models and simulations for defense and automotive applications.
Assist with data analysis, experimentation, testing, and evaluation of vehicle or system performance.
Collaborate with research scientists, engineers, program managers, and other technical stakeholders.
Research emerging defense, mobility, autonomy, simulation, and vehicle technologies.
Prepare technical presentations, research summaries, reports, and other project documentation.
Participate in technical reviews and communicate progress, findings, risks, and recommendations.
Identify opportunities to apply research outcomes to future GM products, systems, and defense programs.
Support university, government, national laboratory, and industry research partnerships as appropriate.
Follow applicable requirements for export controls, intellectual property, and controlled unclassified information.
Contribute to a collaborative, inclusive, and technically rigorous research environment.
More About Who You Are
Curious, analytical, and motivated to solve challenging problems at the intersection of engineering, technology, and national security.
Comfortable learning new technical domains and working across multiple disciplines.
Strong interest or passion for defense related products.
Able to communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
Interested in applied research and in transitioning research findings into practical vehicle, system, or software capabilities.
Able to work independently while seeking guidance and collaborating effectively with a research team.
Committed to responsible handling of sensitive, proprietary, and potentially classified information.
Required Qualifications:
U.S. Citizenship is required
Pursuit of an advanced degree (Masters or PhD) degree in engineering, computer science, applied mathematics, physics, or a related technical field
Must be a current student
Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months
Demonstrated academic, research, project, or internship experience in at least one relevant area, such as modeling and simulation, vehicle systems, autonomous systems, robotics, controls, human-machine interaction, power systems, electrification, systems engineering, or defense technology.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, and technical writing skills.
Ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with scientists, engineers, and program stakeholders.
Ability to work in a hybrid environment and meet project milestones during the summer internship.
Preferred Qualifications:
Currently pursuing a Ph.D. in engineering, computer science, applied mathematics, physics, or a related technical field.
Prior research, coursework, project, or internship experience involving defense systems, military platforms, ground vehicles, simulation, experimentation, testing, or assessment.
Experience with one or more of the following: autonomous systems, vehicle dynamics, vehicle performance, force-on-force simulation, crew-compartment simulation, human-machine interaction, user experience, advanced powertrain, electrification, or power systems.
Experience with programming, data analysis, numerical methods, or simulation tools.
Experience presenting technical work through publications, posters, conference presentations, or project reviews.
Familiarity with systems engineering, requirements development, verification and validation, or technology transition.
Active U.S. Security Clearance as of the first day of work.

posting.title: Radio Frequency Test Engineer Intern
posting.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB
Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.
ABOUT ROCKET LAB
Rocket Lab is a global leader in launch and space systems. We're opening access to space to improve life on Earth through our Electron rocket and Neutron launch vehicle programs, alongside our space systems business. From pioneering carbon composite rocket technology to delivering reliable and rapid launch services, we're pushing the boundaries of what's possible in aerospace.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We're looking for a motivated intern to join our RF (Radio Frequency) Development team at our Auckland Production Complex. As an RF Test Engineering Intern, you will play an important role in the certification of the RF systems used to support Rocket Lab's Neutron launch vehicle.
You will work closely with RF system and RF test engineers to qualify RF components against the demands of re-use and national security programs. This role offers hands-on experience with cutting-edge RF technology while contributing to the development of our next-generation launch vehicle.
This is an opportunity to work on real space technology projects and contribute to missions that are literally reaching for the stars.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
RF Test Engineering:
Work with a portfolio of RF components, including radios, amplifiers, passives, and antennas
Define test campaigns for RF components based on regulatory and customer requirements
Collaborate across RF, Avionics, and Manufacturing teams to develop fit-for-purpose test campaigns
Adapt or build test assets for executing your test campaigns
Lead execution of qualification testing, including S-parameters, noise figure, thermal cycling, vibration, shock, and leakage testing
Support the qualification of RF systems for reusable launch vehicle applications
Document test results and contribute to technical reports
General Responsibilities:
Take ownership for completion of tasks personally delivering results
Commit to and complete tasks within expected time frame, holding yourself accountable
Manage your own task list and execute allocated tasks to assigned deadlines
Communicate effectively with peers using appropriate mediums (email, tickets, meetings)
Support specific tasks for other teammates when asked and appropriately trained
Participate in identifying business challenges and contributing to solutions
Ensure health and safety policies and standard operating procedures are followed
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
MUST HAVE:
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Communications Engineering, RF Engineering, or equivalent
Hands-on experience with RF test equipment (signal generators, VNAs, spectrum analyzers)
Knowledge of transmission line theory
Ability to apply engineering and industry concepts and theories
Strong problem-solving skills and ability to navigate technical challenges
Takes ownership and accountability for task completion by delivering results
Positive attitude and "How can I help?" mentality
Self-managed and committed to working in a fast-paced environment
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to work collaboratively across multiple teams
Can listen and internalize all sides of technical discussions
Proactive communicator, comfortable seeking help when needed to get unblocked
Professional and positive communication skills
NICE TO HAVE:
Experience with RF component qualification testing
Understanding of aerospace RF systems and requirements
Familiarity with regulatory and customer RF requirements (e.g., FCC, RTCA DO-160)
Experience with environmental testing (thermal, vibration, shock)
Knowledge of RF measurement techniques and best practices
Experience with test automation or scripting
Familiarity with CAD tools for RF design
Passion for aerospace, space technology, and innovation
WHAT WE OFFER
Hands-on experience working on real aerospace RF systems for launch vehicles
Mentorship from world-class RF and avionics engineers
Exposure to cutting-edge RF technology and testing methodologies
Professional development opportunities in the space industry
Collaborative and innovative work environment at our Auckland Production Complex
Direct contribution to Rocket Lab's Neutron launch vehicle program
Experience working on reusable launch vehicle technology and national security programs
Opportunity to contribute to missions that make a difference
Potential pathway to future career opportunities at Rocket Lab
ADDITIONAL INFORMATION
Domestic and international travel may be required
Must be able to wear correct PPE in designated areas
Must report near-misses and incidents promptly
Additional duties as reasonably required
HOW TO APPLY
Please ensure you submit a cover letter, detailing why you are interested in the specific role you have applied for. Please make sure to cite a project/experience/hobby that is relevant to the role.
Application Deadline: Friday, 28th August 2026
Please note: We will be reviewing and interviewing candidates on a rolling basis as applications are received. We strongly encourage you to submit your application as early as possible, as positions may be filled before the closing date.
Start Date: November 2026
WHAT TO EXPECT
We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way.
Important information:
FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN US OFFICES ONLY:
To conform to U.S. Government space technology export regulations, including the International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR), Rocket Lab Employees must be a U.S. citizen, lawful U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum, or be eligible to obtain the required authorizations from the U.S. Department of State and/or the U.S. Department of Commerce, as applicable. Learn more about ITAR
here
.

This policy applies to all terms and conditions of employment at Rocket Lab, including recruiting, hiring, placement, promotion, termination, layoff, recall, transfer, leaves of absence, compensation, and training.
Applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation for the application/interview process for a job in the United States should contact Giulia Johnson at
g.biow@rocketlabusa.com.
This dedicated resource is intended solely to assist job seekers with disabilities whose disability prevents them from being able to apply/interview. Only messages left for this purpose will be considered. A response to your request may take up to two business days.
FOR CANDIDATES SEEKING TO WORK IN NEW ZEALAND OFFICES ONLY:
For security reasons, background checks will be undertaken prior to any employment offers being made to an applicant.  These checks will include nationality checks as it is a requirement of this position that you be eligible to access equipment and data regulated by the United States' International Traffic in Arms Regulations.

posting.title: Hardware Technical Program Management Intern
posting.description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a highly motivated and organized Hardware Technical Program Management (TPM) Intern to join our Hardware team. This role is critical in supporting our engineering builds by ensuring the timely and accurate management and tracking of hardware parts and materials, as well as helping to keep the build process running smoothly. As an intern, you will contribute directly to the efficiency and success of our hardware development cycles, working closely with engineers and cross-functional teams.



What You’ll Do

 - Manage and track the inventory of hardware parts and materials required for various engineering builds.

 - Track build issues and help unblock problems, acting as a critical liaison between engineering and external teams.

 - Coordinate with the Hardware Engineering and Procurement teams to ensure parts are ordered and delivered on schedule to meet build timelines.

 - Implement and maintain a systematic tracking process for all components, from initial order through to deployment in the build.

 - Identify and flag potential material shortages or delays, proactively communicating risks to the engineering team.

 - Support continuous improvement efforts for the parts management and inventory control processes to increase efficiency.



What You'll Bring

 - Hands-on experience bringing next-gen battery into production.

 - Strong organizational and interpersonal skills to coordinate across multiple teams and stakeholders.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

posting.title: Autonomy Engineer Intern, Simulation & Robotics, 2027 (HQ)
posting.description:
Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions.


ABOUT THE ROLE:

The core of our system is the computer vision algorithms that allow drones to understand the world around them. You will architect and implement the algorithms that run on every drone powered by Skydio as part of a world class computer vision and deep learning team with researchers who have pushed the state of the art in academia and industry.

As a Research Intern, you will be paired up with one or more members of our core software development team, assuming direct ownership of a project that meaningfully advances the capabilities of our team and products.

If you have a strong foundation in math, theory, and software development and you are interested in directly contributing to the development of the next generation of autonomy algorithms and pushing them into real products, we would love to hear from you.

 


AREAS OF RESPONSIBILITY:

 - Core Simulator Architecture: Design, implement, and evolve the foundational architecture of the Skydio Simulator, ensuring it scales across vehicle types, environments, and use cases.

 - Physics and Dynamics: Improve and extend physics models governing vehicle motion, interactions with the environment, and dynamic agents.

 - Sensor and Hardware Simulation: Build high-fidelity simulations of cameras, IMUs, and other onboard components, including timing, noise characteristics, and hardware behavior.

 - Autonomy Stack Integration: Run and validate the full Skydio autonomy stack in simulation, ensuring consistency between simulated and real-world behavior.

 - Feature Development on Top of the Core: Implement simulator capabilities that unlock new workflows for customers and internal autonomy engineers, from training scenarios to advanced testing modes.

 - Performance and Fidelity: Profile, optimize, and improve simulator performance while continuously pushing realism and accuracy.


WHAT YOU’LL DO:

 - Develop core simulator components in C++ and Python, working close to real-time constraints.

 - Collaborate with autonomy, perception, and controls engineers to align simulation behavior with real-world systems.

 - Debug complex interactions between physics, sensors, autonomy logic, and rendering.

 - Help shape the long-term technical direction of the simulator as both a product and an internal platform.

 - Contribute to documentation and shared understanding of how the simulator works internally.


QUALIFICATIONS:

 - Strong software engineering experience with C++ and Python.

 - Experience building complex systems where performance, determinism, or correctness matter.

 - Comfort reasoning about time-synchronized systems, state machines, or real-time execution.

 - Ability to work in a large, evolving codebase with multiple stakeholders.

 - Interest in robotics, simulation, or physical systems (prior robotics experience is a plus, not a requirement).


BONUS EXPERIENCE:

 - Robotics, simulation, game engines, or real-time systems.

 - Physics engines, sensor modeling, or hardware abstraction layers.

 - Multithreaded or low-latency system design.

 - Experience debugging systems that span software and physical behavior.

Compensation: The hourly rate for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Masters, and $70/hr for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. In addition to base salary, Skydio full-time employees are eligible to enroll in our benefit plans and take advantage of a variety of incentives and stipends.

posting.description:
Job Description
About the Job
Join General Motors Research & Development as a Summer Research Intern supporting the Vehicle Defense Research group within the Safety, Engineering and Defense Research Lab. In this role, you will contribute to applied research involving military systems, defense technology, vehicle platforms, and emerging technologies.
You will work with experienced research scientists and engineers to evaluate current and emerging defense capabilities, apply evidence-based analysis, and help translate research concepts into vehicle, system, and software applications for federal and defense customers.
This internship is designed for a current undergraduate student who has a strong interest in defense technology and a demonstrated knowledge of, and passion for, military systems.
The Role
As a Summer Research Intern, you will support research planning and execution across defense-focused technical domains. You will collaborate with GM researchers, engineers, and external partners to conduct research, support technical analyses, document findings, and communicate recommendations.
You may contribute to projects involving:
Military systems and Soldier systems
Ground vehicle platforms, mobility, and performance
Emerging warfare concepts and defense technology trends
Modeling, simulation, and experimentation
Defense software and hardware systems
Vehicle safety, testing, and assessment
Human-machine interaction and user experience
Autonomous systems and advanced vehicle technologies
The specific project assignment will depend on business needs, your academic background, and your technical interests.
What You’ll Do:
Support research projects by gathering information, conducting analysis, and documenting methods and results.
Research military systems, defense technologies, vehicle platforms, and emerging warfare trends.
Assist with technical assessments of current and proposed R&D projects for defense applications.
Support modeling, simulation, testing, experimentation, and evaluation activities as appropriate.
Collaborate with research scientists, engineers, program managers, and other technical stakeholders.
Prepare technical presentations, research summaries, reports, and project documentation.
Participate in technical reviews and communicate research progress, findings, and recommendations.
Help identify opportunities to apply research outcomes to future GM products, systems, and defense programs.
Support university, government, national laboratory, and industry research partnerships as appropriate.
Assist with identifying dual-use applications for technologies relevant to both civilian and military systems.
Follow applicable requirements for classified information, export controls, intellectual property, and controlled unclassified information.
Contribute to a collaborative, inclusive, and technically rigorous research environment.
More About Who You Are
Passionate about military systems, defense technology, and national security applications.
Curious, analytical, and motivated to understand how complex systems operate in real-world environments.
Interested in applied research and the transition of research findings into practical vehicle, system, or software capabilities.
Comfortable learning new technical domains and working across multiple disciplines.
Able to communicate technical concepts clearly to both technical and nontechnical audiences.
Able to work independently while seeking guidance and collaborating effectively with a research team.
Committed to responsible handling of sensitive, proprietary, and potentially classified information.
Required Qualifications:
U.S. Citizenship is required
Pursuit of a Bachelor’s degree in one of the following areas: engineering, computer science, physics, mathematics, military science, national security, or a related technical or defense-focused field.
Must be a current student
Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months
Demonstrated knowledge of and passion for military systems, defense technology, military operations, or related subjects through coursework, research, projects, military experience, extracurricular activities, or personal study.
Strong analytical, problem-solving, research, and technical writing skills.
Ability to communicate and collaborate effectively with scientists, engineers, military stakeholders, and program managers.
Ability to work in a hybrid environment and meet project milestones during the summer internship.
Preferred Qualifications:
Currently pursuing, or planning to pursue, a master’s degree or Ph.D. in engineering, computer science, physics, mathematics, military science, national security, or a related field.
Prior research, coursework, project, internship, or military experience involving defense systems, military platforms, high performance ground vehicles, simulation, experimentation, testing, or assessment.
Familiarity with vehicle systems, defense acquisition, systems engineering, requirements development, verification and validation, or technology transition.
Experience with programming, data analysis, modeling, simulation, numerical methods, or technical visualization.
Experience presenting technical work through publications, posters, conference presentations, project reviews, or competitions.
Experience with one or more of the following: vehicle performance, autonomous systems, robotics, controls, human-machine interaction, defense software, advanced powertrain, electrification, or power systems.
Experience with automotive research, testing, or development.

posting.title: 2027 Supply Chain Intern
posting.description:
Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
The intern positions will support the Supply Chain group in strategic planning, long-term supplier selection and negotiations. This position requires the ability to work with procurement, engineering, finance and legal teams and third parties such as suppliers. The position requires interest in industry dynamics, business negotiation and pricing, manufacturing processes, and risk mitigation.
Domain Areas and Key Responsibilities
– The intern will collaborate and support in the development and rollout of various business solutions within the following areas:
Demand & Material Planning
– Support enhancement and optimization of our MRP system inputs/outputs/engine-logic and integration into all ERP modules, develop analytics/dashboards. Identifying material gaps and supplier risk, aid the configuration team with BOM errors, sparing contract requirements and SC master data requirements, support the Program team with right-to-left planning and supply chain milestone checkoff procedures.
Procurement
– Optimize an RFQ system and upstream data flows into the Supply Chain landscape. Develop tools to support multi-tier quoting, advanced sourcing, enhanced Supplier Collaboration and Interaction. Build Sourcing & Cost Trajectory analyses and insight tools.
Purchasing
– Support the Buying team with specific Purchasing SOPs and training material, troubleshoot Part/BOM issues, develop part availability tracking dashboards and ad-hoc analytics, enhance the deployed Purchase Request process to better automate Purchasing workflows and traceability, etc.
Logistics, Warehouse & Supplier Quality
– Optimize WMS/QMS systems and associated integrated processes to enhance inventory accuracy and build readiness. Support compliance and sparing audits. Work with System teams with Inventory analytics for period-end/ad-hoc requests.
Operational Scale & Supply Chain Health
– Document Supply Chain processes (both for internal SMEs and external Supplier collaborators) and develop Doc change control and rollout procedures, support in developing a comprehensive Supplier Scorecard and integrate it into the Supplier Portal system landscape, develop a risk assessment supplier profile and health-check mechanism to enable scale and risk mitigation, aid the development of Compliance Requirements related to Federal and/or Industry-specific regulations and guidelines. Develop and Manage Supply Chain Onboarding material and checklists.
Miscellaneous/Collaborative
–
Liaise between Business and IT groups to gather and clarify requirements, support sprint planning and end-user testing and training.
Perform end-user application/system/process testing and report out.
Support the effort to develop a global and comprehensive Supply Chain digital ecosystem pipeline and capability roadmap.
Collaborate with Data team with data flow triage and issue-resolution intended to enable streamlined and accurate analytics.
Develop a strong familiarity with the Supply Chain end-user base and their data and system usage and feedback to gather enhancement requirements for ad-hoc problem solving and building into the overall roadmap.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Business Analytics, Information Technology & Systems Architecture, Software Engineer, Computer Science, or any related field.
Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester.
Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program.
Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in one of our offices in summer 2027.
PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS
Proficiency in a variety of programming languages such as Go, Java, C++, Python, JavaScript, etc
Experience with Microsoft Excel, Spark, PySpark, SQL (T-SQL Postgres), Enterprise Data Systems like Palantir Foundry
Experience with AWS, Azure, or GCP security ecosystem, containerization, and associated tooling.
Knowledge of connecting external APIs
Knowledge of data & visualization tools, such as Tableau

Experience with Solid Modeling using a major CAD package, NX or CREO preferred

Ability to learn to read a 2D drawing and interpret design intent in a 3D Environment
Computer literacy – knowledgeable in MS Office, Windows, and Adobe Acrobat

posting.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Mechanical Engineering - Michigan
posting.description:
Work Flexibility: Onsite
What You Get Out of the Internship
​​
At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will: ​ ​
Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting​
Implement new ideas, be constantly challenged, and develop your skills​
Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business​
Be a part of an innovative team and culture​
Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format
Who we want
​​
Challengers.
People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions.​
Teammates.
Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward.​
Charismatic networkers.
Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts.​
Strategic thinkers.
Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives.​
Customer-oriented achievers.
Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships.​
Game changers.
Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better.
Opportunities Available
​
​As a Mechanical Engineering intern at Stryker, you will be placed in one of the following teams:
Research & Development
New Product Development
R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products.  They research new technologies, customer expectations, business requirements and regulations.  They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts.  These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production.
Product Engineering
R&D interns in Product Engineering work with cross-functional teams to identify the greatest needs for improvements on current products.  They research new technologies, customer feedback, and product performance data to make our products better for Stryker and for our customers.  Product Engineering interns work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, Test Labs, and root cause analysis methods.  These interns utilize their technical education to improve the safety and efficacy of our existing products.
Test Lab
Test interns partner closely with Test Engineers and R&D to experiment with early prototypes and vet out product designs throughout the design process.  What this really means is that we get to be the Mythbusters of our division.  You think your design can last the entire expected service life? We put it to the test.  Just like the show, we quickly design and build fixtures to simulate real life situations. In addition to these experiments, we are ultimately responsible for design verification – the quantitative testing of the technical specifications of the product.  A team’s experience ranges from 2 to over 15 years with technical specialties ranging from sterilization, mechanical, electrical, software, and optics.  If you’re the type of person that has the magic ability to break things – we want you!
Majors Targeted:
Mechanical Engineering, or related majors
$20 min hourly wage – $35 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location
What You Need
​​
Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in a related field; must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship.​
Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above (verified at time of hire)
Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require employment-based sponsorship now or in the future.​
Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships
Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities
Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment.
Travel Percentage: None
Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, ethnicity, color, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status. Stryker is an EO employer – M/F/Veteran/Disability.
Stryker Corporation will not discharge or in any other manner discriminate against employees or applicants because they have inquired about, discussed, or disclosed their own pay or the pay of another employee or applicant. However, employees who have access to the compensation information of other employees or applicants as a part of their essential job functions cannot disclose the pay of other employees or applicants to individuals who do not otherwise have access to compensation information, unless the disclosure is (a) in response to a formal complaint or charge, (b) in furtherance of an investigation, proceeding, hearing, or action, including an investigation conducted by the employer, or (c) consistent with the contractor’s legal duty to furnish information.

posting.description:
Job Description Summary
Job Description
University Student Intern – Hot Gas Path Value Engineering & Project Management
Job Description
This University Student Intern role will be a key contributor within the Product Management function supporting the Pivot to Value (P2V) Hot Gas Path (HGP) Value Engineering team. The Intern will support strategic initiatives focused on improving safety, quality, delivery, cost, and capacity across GE Vernova’s Gas Turbine Hot Gas Path product portfolio, including blades, nozzles, shrouds, and near flow path seal (NFPS) components.
Working alongside Product Managers, Value Engineers, Design Engineering, Manufacturing, Sourcing, Supply Chain, Repair, Quality, and Field Services teams, the Intern will participate in projects that drive value optimization, cost reduction, manufacturability improvements, lifecycle cost reduction, and execution excellence for HGP parts. This role provides an opportunity to gain hands-on experience supporting component-level value engineering while learning how engineering, supply chain, manufacturing, repair, and commercial teams collaborate to deliver customer value.
Value Engineering is a practice focused on identifying and implementing solutions that optimize product value through improved design, manufacturing efficiency, repairability, sourcing strategies, quality enhancement, and cost reduction. The Intern will support these efforts through project coordination, cost analysis, data management, business case support, and engineering-focused problem solving across the HGP portfolio.
Roles and Responsibilities
Support Value Engineering initiatives for Gas Turbine Hot Gas Path components, including blades, nozzles, shrouds, and related high-temperature hardware.
Assist Senior Engineers and Value Engineering leaders with project execution related to design optimization, manufacturability, sourcing alternatives, repair strategies, lifecycle cost reduction, and capacity improvement.
Gather and analyze cost, manufacturing, field execution, supplier, repair, quality, and operational data to support business cases, project prioritization, and value capture.
Track schedules, milestones, risks, action items, financials, and value realization metrics across multiple projects using project management tools, dashboards, and reporting systems.
Collaborate with Design Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Sourcing, Quality, Repair, and Field Services teams to identify and implement improvements that reduce cost, cycle time, COPQ, and total lifecycle cost while improving quality, yield, productivity, and delivery performance.
Participate in value engineering workshops, cost-out ideation sessions, continuous improvement events, and gated Value Engineering process activities from idea generation through execution tracking and value realization.
Prepare project reviews, stakeholder updates, executive-level presentations, standard work, process documentation, lessons learned, and best-practice repositories.
Learn and apply Value Engineering methodologies, project management principles, cost optimization practices, and engineering-focused problem solving.
Required Qualifications
Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Supply Chain Management, Operations, Business, or a related technical discipline.
Sophomore standing or above with at least one academic term remaining following completion of the Co-Op assignment.
Demonstrated academic achievement and interest in engineering, manufacturing, project management, or operations.
Ability to work full-time during the Co-Op assignment period.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Interest in power generation equipment, gas turbine technology, high-temperature components, manufacturing operations, repair processes, and field services.
Excellent organizational and project coordination abilities.
Strong verbal and written communication skills.
Ability to manage multiple assignments while working in a fast-paced environment.
Experience with Microsoft Excel, PowerPoint, Power BI, or similar data analysis tools.
Familiarity with project management concepts and methodologies.
Ability to analyze data and present findings in a clear and concise manner.
Demonstrated teamwork and collaboration skills.
Strong attention to detail and commitment to delivering high-quality work.
Interest in cost analysis, business case development, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.
Basic understanding of manufacturing processes, engineering drawings, and industrial equipment is preferred.
Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement methodologies is a plus.
Passion for learning and working alongside experienced engineering and business leaders.
What You Will Gain
Exposure to GE Vernova’s Gas Turbine Hot Gas Path product portfolio, Value Engineering organization, and cross-functional cost-out processes.
Hands-on experience supporting HGP component value engineering, cost-out, manufacturability, repairability, and sourcing improvement projects.
Practical experience with project management, business case development, cost tracking, and value realization across a complex engineering product portfolio.
Opportunity to work directly with Senior Engineers, Product Managers, Manufacturing Leaders, Sourcing, Supply Chain, Repair, Quality, and Field Services teams.
Experience developing business cases and supporting value creation initiatives.

Exposure to continuous improvement, capacity growth, operational excellence, and Value Engineering methodologies within the power generation industry.
This Intern position offers a unique opportunity to develop technical, business, and leadership skills while contributing to meaningful projects that improve Hot Gas Path product value, component cost, manufacturability, repairability, quality, and operational execution.

40-50 hours per week with set hourly salary based on year in school

Interest in entrepreneurship

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
About This Role
Summer internships will range between the months of May and August.
All dates
dependent upon the university schedule of the selected students. Internships are full-time and on-site in Los Angeles, CA.
The GNC (Guidance, Navigation & Controls) team is responsible for the design, analysis, simulation, and operational performance of Varda’s reentry vehicles. In this internship, you'll help enable end-to-end GNC performance for our flight vehicles—supporting everything from 6DOF simulation and control system modeling to sensor integration and trajectory optimization.
Internships at Varda are optimal for students looking to grow technically and professionally while working on impactful projects critical to the company’s success. You will be working on a collaborative team in a startup environment while being able to learn from some of most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the world. We’re dedicated to providing an experience that will let your decisions and contributions help drive Varda’s success.
Responsibilities
As part of the GNC team, own or contribute to analysis, algorithms and simulations for reentry vehicles
Own Integration and testing of GNC sensors, actuators and software in simulation and hardware in the loop environments
Design and implement mission critical tooling needed to facilitate automated maneuver responsibility and scheduling decisions

R&D interns in New Product Development work with cross-functional teams to identify the needs and the goals of future products.  They research new technologies, customer expectations, business requirements and regulations.  They may work with a variety of tools, including CAD, FEA, and our Test Labs to develop new product concepts.  These interns utilize their technical education to design new products and drive them from concept to production.
