Description
At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history.
Northrop Grumman is a space pioneer, supporting government, civil and commercial customers in solving their biggest challenges. Our forward-leaning, innovative spirit is backed by a legacy of expertise that began at the dawn of the space age. Our mission experience in space runs deep, we know our customers well, and our capabilities are unmatched. This is what allows us to provide reliable, agile and affordable space solutions to best serve our customers.
From defending freedom to advancing human discovery, we are defining what is possible in space every day.
An internship at Northrop Grumman is unique. Sure, you’ll learn new skills, explore our enterprise, network with experts, connect with thought leaders, and finish with a resume that opens doors. But you’ll gain something even more valuable: pride in what you’ve done. Join us and launch your career. We’ll support you with training, professional development and networking opportunities, and our shared vision of global security.
Northrop Grumman is seeking Structural Engineers for an internship opportunity.
This position will be located at our Space sector in
San Diego, CA.
The qualified candidate will become part of Northrop Grumman’s Mission Enabling Products Business Unit.
Roles and Responsibilities
Participate in/lead analysis group continuous improvement and training efforts
Compile material allowable and property data to support analysis database creation
Organize and archive analysis group technical data and documentation
Build finite element models and perform trade studies and analysis to support program schedules
Basic Qualifications
A candidate must meet ALL of the below criteria. The candidate must:
Be a student who is enrolled full-time and pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree from an accredited college/university and will be enrolled full time in Fall 2027
Be majoring in a Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering degree
Be available to work full-time (40 hours per week) for at least 10 weeks during
summer 2027.
Be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance (U.S. citizenship is a pre-requisite) as well as Program Special access within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the company to meet its business needs (U.S. citizenship is a pre-requisite)
Some finite element, mechanics of materials, dynamics, and vibrations coursework completed
Experience and success working within teams
Proven ability to multi-task and self-starter able to work independently
Strong interpersonal skills to drive actions necessary to accomplish assigned tasks
Strong organizational skills in managing time, projects and resources
Technical attention to detail on past projects and assignments
Preferred Qualifications:
Have an overall cumulative GPA of 3.00/4.0 or higher
Basic knowledge of Lean Manufacturing principles
Prior leadership experience
Intern Pay Range:
Bachelor’s: $21.50 to $39.00 per hour
Master’s: $30.50 to $48.00 per hour
At Northrop Grumman, our internship pay rates are standardized and take into account three main factors: the anticipated graduation date of the individual, the cost of labor of the geographic location, and whether the internship is considered technical or administrative.

posting.title: Data Engineering Intern
posting.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB
Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.
ABOUT THE ROLE
We're looking for a motivated intern to join our Operational Data team in Auckland. Operational Data is a software engineering team sitting at the intersection between software and data. The team develops and maintains the tools and services that extract value from operational data, enabling engineers and analysts to derive the technical insights used to develop and improve Rocket Lab's launch vehicles and space systems.
As a Data Engineering Intern you will learn modern data engineering practices and get hands-on with real data pipelines from across every company domain - from avionics to propulsion, and everything in between. You'll build and maintain the software that collates, curates and surfaces the data our engineering and operations teams rely on every day.
You'll work as part of a sprint team, contributing to code reviews, documentation and backlog refinement, and you'll have the opportunity to demonstrate what you've built directly to the stakeholders who use it. Under the guidance of experienced engineers, you'll take ownership of your own tickets and see your work deployed and supported in a live operational environment.
This is an opportunity to work on real space technology projects and contribute to missions that are literally reaching for the stars.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
Operational Data:
Support the collation, curation and classification of operational data
Support the retrieval and display of operational data
Build and port data pipelines from across the business
Support analysis and report generation on behalf of stakeholders in engineering and operations
Software Development:
Develop software and tooling to support the data management and exploitation needs of the company
Maintain existing software and tooling according to bug-fix and feature requests
Collaborate in the review and approval of merge requests
Document software architecture and designs
Refine product backlog items and keep assigned tickets up to date
Participate in team activities (stand-ups, retrospectives, sprint planning) and contribute innovative ideas
Lead demonstrations of software products to stakeholders
Deploy and support operational software
Collaborate with engineers and team members across multiple departments
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
MUST HAVE:
Studying towards (or recently completed) a tertiary diploma, certificate or degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Engineering Science, or equivalent level of knowledge
Experience with Python development - professional, coursework or personal projects all count
Experience with Git
Excellent problem-solving skills
Ability to work independently and as part of a collaborative team
Team player with a positive attitude and a "how can I help?" mentality
Proven communication skills and the ability to build strong working relationships
Passion for aerospace, space technology, and innovation
NICE TO HAVE:
REST API and services development
Experience with common data analysis libraries and tools, such as Pandas/NumPy, ETL pipelines and SQL
Kubernetes, Docker and/or Linux
Data visualisation
Knowledge of data science and numerical analysis techniques
Previous internship or project experience in software or data engineering
WHAT WE OFFER
Hands-on experience working on real aerospace and space technology projects
Mentorship from world-class engineers and industry professionals
Exposure to data from across the business, from avionics to propulsion
Opportunity to build and deploy production data pipelines and tooling
Professional development opportunities in the space industry
Collaborative and innovative work environment
Opportunity to contribute to missions that make a difference
Potential pathway to future career opportunities at Rocket Lab
HOW TO APPLY

posting.title: Summer 2027 Software Engineering Internship/Co-op
posting.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.
SUMMER 2027 SOFTWARE ENGINEERING INTERNSHIP/CO-OP
SpaceX seeks extraordinary students to join us for software engineering roles in Summer 2027. As a software intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees who will help you apply your knowledge and grow your skills on projects that have a significant impact. You’ll also get to have some fun and network with other interns and employees through optional social and professional events. If you’ve demonstrated a commitment to academic success and motivation to apply your knowledge outside of the classroom, you are a great candidate! Aerospace experience is not required to be successful here - rather we look for smart, motivated, collaborative engineers who love solving problems and want to make an impact on a super inspiring mission.
Internships are available with a variety of software engineering teams across the company at Bastrop, TX; Brownsville, TX; Cape Canaveral, FL; Hawthorne (Los Angeles), CA; Irvine, CA; McGregor (Waco), TX; Palo Alto, CA; and Redmond (Seattle), WA.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s degree or graduate program
3+ months of software programming or development experience
Software coding experience in one or more of the following: C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, Python
Applicant for this intern position must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (e.g., green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158.
PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
GPA of 3.5 or above
6+ months experience developing and deploying software that has been used on real-world applications and projects
Strong fundamental knowledge of computer architecture and networks
Experience with software documentation, creating system diagrams, and enumerating software requirements
Strong skills in debugging, performance optimization and unit testing
Strong interpersonal skills (examples: leading a student organization or working successfully in teams)
Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements
Ability to work independently and in a team, take initiative, and communicate effectively
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Able to work full time, onsite for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning in May or June 2027
Able to provide own transportation for positions at Brownsville, Cape Canaveral and McGregor locations
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
Pay Range:
Software Engineering Intern/Freshman/Sophomore: $30.00/hour
Software Engineering Intern/Junior/Senior: $34.00/hour
Software Engineering Intern/Completed Bachelor's: $36.00/hour
Software Engineering Intern/Completed Master's: $38.00/hour
Software Engineering Intern/Completed PhD: $40.00/hour
Your salary will be determined by academic level. Pay is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs, as well as access to our comprehensive medical coverage and a 401(k) retirement plan. Students joining SpaceX through our internship program will receive the opportunity to attend presentations from company leaders, social and networking events, as well as professional and personal development trainings. Interns are also eligible for paid company holidays. SpaceX offers 10 or more paid holidays per year.
PROGRAM DESCRIPTION:
VEHICLE
DRAGON
: The Dragon spacecraft is capable of carrying up to 7 passengers to and from Earth orbit, and beyond. It is the only spacecraft currently flying that is capable of returning significant amounts of cargo to Earth and is the first private spacecraft to take humans to the space station.
FALCON
: The Falcon program tackles space exploration’s toughest problems through the ongoing development of our reusable launch vehicles, Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy. These vehicles are currently responsible for delivering commercial, national security, and NASA satellites into orbit, as well as supply critical science, supplies, and crew to the International Space Station.
STARSHIP:
The Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket – collectively referred to as Starship – represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond. Starship is the world’s most powerful launch vehicle ever developed, designed to carry more than 100 metric tonnes to orbit in a fully reusable configuration and powered by our Raptor and Raptor Vacuum (RVac) engines, which are designed for use in the vacuum of space.
SATELLITE / SPACEXAI
STARLINK:
Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, including thousands of satellites, consumer receivers, and the software that brings it all together. Our Starlink teams are also undertaking SpaceX's next-generation mobile network, Starlink Mobile, connecting human beings all around the globe anywhere they can see the sky.
STARSHIELD

SPACEXAI -
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. This includes Grok, the frontier AI model for everything you need, trained on the world's largest supercluster, and developing Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth.

posting.title: Supply Chain Tooling Engineer Intern
posting.description:
ABOUT BASE

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Base is building a vertically-integrated residential energy company — hardware, software, and field operations all under one roof. As a Supply Chain Tooling & Optimization Intern, you'll work directly with the teams standing up our internally built TMS, WMS, and MRP and scaling deployments across Texas. This is not a shadowing internship: you'll own real problems at the intersection of manufacturing, logistics, and software, building the tools and the intelligent layers on top of them that help us install batteries faster and more reliably.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Build internal tools, dashboards, and trackers that increase visibility across the supply chain.

 - Contribute to our internally built TMS, WMS, and MRP — wiring up data pipelines, integrations, and the models behind them.

 - Analyze operational data from ERP, supplier portals, and shipping systems to surface bottlenecks, blocked orders, and disruptions.

 - Prototype inventory and network optimization — multi-site / multi-warehouse stock optimization, warehouse slotting, and staffing/labor planning.

 - Build first-pass forecasting models for material demand (to feed MRP planning parameters) and for the reliability of supplier commitments — how likely a supplier is to actually hit committed dates and quantities.

 - Ship these inside the tools planners already use, not as notebooks on a shelf — and reach for the simplest method that works.

 - Partner directly with planners, buyers, and ops managers to scope small MVPs, deploy frequently, and iterate on real feedback.
   


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Currently pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Industrial/Systems Engineering, Operations Research, Supply Chain, Data Science, or similar.

 - Comfort writing Python and SQL, and a genuine interest in building tools — not just analyzing data.

 - Some exposure to at least one of: optimization / operations research or basic ML / anomaly detection (coursework, projects, or prior internships all count).

 - Familiarity with data analysis and dashboarding; bonus for experience with pipelines, APIs, or ERP systems.

 - Strong written and verbal communication — able to translate between technical and non-technical stakeholders.

 - Builder mindset — enjoys ambiguity, takes ownership, and is excited to make things work better, not just measure them.

 - Experience in a tech-enabled operations environment is a plus— energy, logistics, or manufacturing.




ABOUT THE TEAM

Our Supply Chain team tackles the challenge of sourcing battery cells, assembling high-capacity packs, and forging vendor partnerships to produce and deliver the industry's lowest-cost, highest-quality home battery systems at unprecedented scale.

By optimizing landed costs through strategic global sourcing, domestic manufacturing ramp-up, and durable supplier relationships, your work directly powers Base Power's mission of advancing human prosperity through energy abundance - delivering reliable whole-home backup and below-market electricity rates to tens of thousands of households.

These efforts drive uniquely massive impact by fueling one of America's fastest-growing distributed virtual power plants, already exceeding 200 MWh deployed and aggregating flexible storage to bolster the grid against surging demands from AI, electrification, and extreme weather. Exceptional candidates will seize the chance to build the supply foundation for a company raising billions to manufacture in-house and expand nationally, achieving grid-scale resilience at speeds and costs no traditional player can replicate.



Please note: Base is a startup, which means priorities shift and evolve quickly. Your role may expand or change based on the needs of the business at any given time, so the responsibilities listed may not be exhaustive.




OUR VALUES

 - First Principles Thinking: Question assumptions. Principles > rules.

 - Operate at Base Pace: Focus on what matters, act quickly, and learn by doing.

 - Give & Get Feedback: Be direct, be humble, and maintain a growth mindset.

 - Everyone’s an Owner: Follow through on commitments and own results.

 - Strong Opinions, Loosely Held: Drive clarity and make calls with imperfect information.

 - Committed to the Mission: Rebuilding the grid is a big challenge. We work hard because we care deeply about the impact we’re creating. We work in-person. It’s not a 9-to-5. We are all-in.

 - Fun & Optimism Coexist with Grit: Collaboration and celebration coincide with the intensity of building real things.
   
   


DO THE BEST WORK OF YOUR LIFE AT BASE.

posting.description:
SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.
SPRING 2027 GRADUATE ENGINEER
As a Graduate Engineer, you will be responsible for working on creative solutions to real aerospace challenges. This is not an ordinary “internship” – you will be given as much responsibility as our full-time engineers and will be an integral part of the team. If you’ve demonstrated a commitment to academic success and motivation to apply your knowledge outside of the classroom, you are a great candidate!
Internships are available with a variety of engineering teams across the company including design, manufacturing and operations at Bastrop, TX; Bloomfield, CT, Brownsville, TX; Cape Canaveral, FL; Hawthorne (Los Angeles), CA; Irvine, CA; Long Beach, CA, McGregor (Waco), TX; Palo Alto, CA; Redmond (Seattle), WA; Vandenberg, CA; and Woodinville, WA.
BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:
6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable)
Enrolled in a graduate program by the start of employment and holds a bachelor’s degree in engineering, physics or math discipline
Applicant for this graduate engineer position must be a (i) U.S. citizen or national, (ii) U.S. lawful permanent resident (e.g., green card holder), (iii) Refugee under 8 U.S.C. § 1157, or (iv) Asylee under 8 U.S.C. § 1158.
PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:
GPA of 3.5 or above
9+ months experience of application of technical skills outside of the classroom (examples: laboratory, research, extracurricular project teams, volunteering, personal projects or prior internship/work experience)
Ability to work well in an integrated collaborative team environment, including frequent interactions with technicians, other engineers, and managers
Ability to work effectively in a dynamic professional setting with changing needs and requirements
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:
Able to work full time, onsite for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning in January or March 2027
Able to provide own transportation for positions at Brownsville, Cape Canaveral, McGregor and Vandenberg locations
COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS:
Pay range:
Graduate Engineer/Completed Bachelor's: $83,200.00/per year
Graduate Engineer/Completed Master's: $91,000.00/per year
Graduate Engineer/Completed PhD: $100,100.00/per year
Your salary will be determined by academic level. Pay is just one part of your total rewards package at SpaceX. You may also be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs, as well as access to our comprehensive medical coverage and a 401(k) retirement plan. Students joining SpaceX through our internship program will receive the opportunity to attend presentations from company leaders, social and networking events, as well as professional and personal development trainings. Interns are also eligible for paid company holidays. SpaceX offers 10 or more paid holidays per year.
PROGRAM DESCRIPTIONS:
VEHICLE
DRAGON
: The Dragon spacecraft is capable of carrying up to 7 passengers to and from Earth orbit, and beyond. It is the only spacecraft currently flying that is capable of returning significant amounts of cargo to Earth and is the first private spacecraft to take humans to the space station.
FALCON
: The Falcon program tackles space exploration’s toughest problems through the ongoing development of our reusable launch vehicles, Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy. These vehicles are currently responsible for delivering commercial, national security, and NASA satellites into orbit, as well as supply critical science, supplies, and crew to the International Space Station.
STARSHIP:
The Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket – collectively referred to as Starship – represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond. Starship is the world’s most powerful launch vehicle ever developed, designed to carry more than 100 metric tonnes to orbit in a fully reusable configuration and powered by our Raptor and Raptor Vacuum (RVac) engines, which are designed for use in the vacuum of space.
SATELLITE / SPACEXAI
STARLINK:
Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and is providing fast, reliable internet to millions of users worldwide. We design, build, test, and operate all parts of the system, including thousands of satellites, consumer receivers, and the software that brings it all together. Our Starlink teams are also undertaking SpaceX's next-generation mobile network, Starlink Mobile, connecting human beings all around the globe anywhere they can see the sky.
STARSHIELD
- Starshield leverages SpaceX’s Starlink technology and launch capability to support national security efforts. While Starlink is designed for consumer and commercial use, Starshield is designed for government use, with an initial focus on earth observation, communications, and hosted payloads.
SPACEXAI -
SpaceXAI’s mission is to create AI systems that can accurately understand the universe and aid humanity in its pursuit of knowledge. This includes Grok, the frontier AI model for everything you need, trained on the world's largest supercluster, and developing Starmind, a new constellation of satellites capturing solar energy in space to power low-cost, high-performance AI compute for Earth.
ITAR REQUIREMENTS:

Base is America’s next-generation power company. We’re rebuilding the foundation of modern civilization–electricity–by deploying a vast network of distributed batteries that is transforming today’s fragile, centralized grid into a resilient and abundant system. We are engineers, operators, and creatives solving some of the most complex, interdisciplinary challenges of our time.




ABOUT THE ROLE

Our marketing team combines creative, customer-focused strategy with data-driven precision to reach the right customers at the right time. We’re hiring an Organic Social Content Manager to build Base into one of the most distinctive, entertaining, and trusted energy brands on social.

You’ll own the day-to-day operation of Base’s organic channels, from developing the content calendar and creating original content to publishing, engaging with our audience, and learning from performance. You’ll turn Base’s products, customers, employees, and mission into platform-native stories people want to watch, share, and join.

This is a hands-on creative role. You’ll develop recurring social series, respond quickly to relevant cultural moments, and personally bring ideas from concept through production. You should be as comfortable scripting and filming a video as you are writing a caption, organizing a calendar, or interpreting performance data.

 


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Own Base’s organic social strategy, content calendar, and publishing cadence across Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, X, and emerging platforms.

 - Develop original, recurring content series that make Base, energy, and the grid interesting, useful, and fun to follow.

 - Concept, script, capture, edit, write, and publish platform-native content, including short-form video, photos, graphics, carousels, and written posts.

 - Find compelling stories across Base’s customers, products, installations, employees, markets, and mission, then turn them into content people want to watch and share.

 - Balance planned programming with reactive content, moving quickly on trends, customer conversations, cultural moments, and company news when Base has something meaningful to add.

 - Maintain the content calendar and manage the workflows behind it, including briefs, assets, approvals, deadlines, and platform-specific adaptations.

 - Collaborate with design, marketing, product, operations, and other teams to support launches, events, market expansions, and major company moments.

 - Build relationships with Base’s audience by responding to comments and messages, amplifying customer stories and user-generated content, and identifying advocates who can help grow the community.

 - Track organic reach, shares, saves, watch time, engagement, audience growth, and the performance of recurring series. Turn those insights into better ideas and stronger future content.

 - Stay close to platform changes, emerging formats, internet culture, and the brands and creators setting the standard for social content.

 


WHAT YOU’LL BRING

 - Experience creating and managing organic social content for a consumer brand, product-led company, creative agency, media company, or similarly fast-moving organization.

 - A portfolio of original social work that demonstrates strong ideas, platform-native execution, and measurable audience or engagement growth.

 - Hands-on content creation skills. You can take an idea from concept to published post, including scripting, filming, editing, copywriting, and packaging it for the platform.

 - Strong short-form video instincts, including hooks, pacing, framing, captions, sound, and storytelling. You are comfortable using mobile-first editing tools such as CapCut, Premiere, or similar software.

 - Excellent writing skills and the ability to make a technical or unfamiliar subject feel clear, human, and interesting.

 - Deep familiarity with Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn, and X, including an understanding of what audiences expect from each platform.

 - Strong creative judgment and a high bar for what is worth publishing. You know how to participate in culture without forcing the brand into conversations where it does not belong.

The Marketing team at Base is lean, high-ownership, and results-driven. We operate with clear accountability, tight feedback loops, and a strong bias toward action. Write data analytic reports

Familiarity with robotics or AV data is a plus

ML
Robotics

Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events

posting.title: Materials Management Intern (Summer 2027 or Year Round)
posting.description:
About Pierce, an Oshkosh company
At Pierce Manufacturing, we build trucks that protect people and communities around the world. To our team, there is no room for anything less than providing the absolute best. Since 1913, building truck bodies on Model T Ford chassis in an old converted church has evolved to creating highly customized, carefully designed and engineering pumpers, aerials, tankers and rescue units that have no equal. Today, you'll find more than
30,000 Pierce apparatuses
on the road that are making a difference in people's lives, every day. To us, every step in the process of building our trucks is personal. From innovation and expertise, to the customization and service. Our trucks are designed to perform under the toughest conditions.
SUMMARY
Assist and support the Materials department within Pierce Manufacturing. This role will utilize analytical skills to identify opportunities and develop solutions that result in optimal material flow at the lowest total landed cost. Develop process improvements within the Materials department.
YOUR IMPACT
These duties are not meant to be all-inclusive and other duties may be assigned:
Compile data from ERP systems, spreadsheet, and other sources to support decision-making in conjunction with the Plan for Every Part process.
Reduce excess material handling inside facilities, between facilities and to and from local suppliers through value stream analysis and application of PFEP principles.
Support standardization, advancement and implementation of a lean enterprise material flow strategy.
Work with the Materials and Operations department to introduce, promote, and implement lean manufacturing techniques to reduce cost and improve efficiency.
Run and compile various reports as well as run various data analytics to understand the data
Assist in the continuous improvement techniques including Continuous Improvement events and 5S.
MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS
Student working towards a Bachelor’s degree in Operations/Manufacturing Management, Business, Engineering, or related field for entire duration of internship.
STANDOUT QUALIFICATIONS
GPA of 3.0 or greater
Excellent organizational, communication, and leadership skills.
Pay Range:
$18.00 - $37.00
The above pay range reflects the minimum and maximum target pay for the position across all U.S. locations. Within this range, individual pay is determined by various factors, including the scope and responsibilities of the role, the candidate's experience, education and skills, as well as the equity of pay among team members in similar positions. Beyond offering a competitive total rewards package, we prioritize a people-first culture and offer various opportunities to support team member growth and success.
Oshkosh is committed to working with and offering reasonable accommodation to job applicants with disabilities. If you need assistance or an accommodation due to disability for any part of the employment process, please contact us at

posting.title: Co-op, DevOps Engineer: January - June 2027 (Hybrid)
posting.description:
Job Summary
Co-op, DevOps Engineer: January - June 2027 (Hybrid)
Position Overview
Position Dates: January 11, 2027 – June 30, 2027
Insulet is seeking a motivated and detail-oriented DevOps Engineer to join our team within our Software Research and Development organization. As an Associate DevOps Engineer you will support the design, maintenance, and operation of continuous integration/continuous deployment pipelines used to build, package, test, and deploy products. Working under the guidance of senior team members, you will help automate repetitive processes, support software release activities, and contribute to continuous improvement across development teams.
Responsibilities
Monitor CI/CD pipeline runs, investigate basic failures, and escalate recurring or complex issues to senior DevOps team members.
Maintain build and deployment documentation, including runbooks, setup steps, and troubleshooting notes for supported tools and environments.
Assist with routine DevOps operational tasks such as access requests, environment checks, release support activities, and tool configuration updates.
Minimum Requirements:
Enrolled in a 4-year undergraduate
Computer Science, Computer Engineering,
or relevant engineering program.
Communication: Clear and effective communication with diverse teams, including developers, operations, and business stakeholders.
Active Listening: Attentively listen to others, demonstrating empathy and understanding.
Proactive: Taking initiative to identify and solve problems before they escalate
Adaptable: Flexibility to adjust strategies and approaches based on changing circumstances and feedback
Skills and Competencies
Foundational understanding of DevOps and configuration management concepts.
Basic scripting experience to help automate repetitive processes, including exposure to tools such as Python, Ant, Gradle, Maven, or similar technologies.
Exposure to source control using Git.
Exposure to repositories such as GitHub, BitBucket, GitLab, or Google Cloud Source Repositories.
Familiarity with CI/CD tools such as Jenkins, Ansible, or GitLab.
Familiarity with functional programming and object-oriented programming concepts.
Familiarity with Linux and Windows operating systems and basic command-line usage.
Exposure to Docker Containers
Education and Experience
Coursework, internship, co-op, or professional exposure to CI/CD pipelines, tools, and infrastructure for applications deployed on premises or in the cloud.
Exposure to software configuration management (SCM) environments, branching strategies, and source control workflows.
Ability to support development, test, integration, and production environments under the guidance of more experienced team members.
Additional Information
The position is hybrid at our Acton office.
This position is not eligible for employer-based visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the U.S. without current or future sponsorship needs.
Additional Information:
Compensation & Benefits:
For U.S.-based positions only, the annual base salary range for this role is $25.00 - $34.00
This position may also be eligible for incentive compensation.
We offer a comprehensive benefits package, including:
• Medical insurance
• Holiday pay
• Sick time off
• And additional employee wellness programs
Application Details:
This job posting will remain open until the position is filled.
To apply, please visit the Insulet Careers site and submit your application online.
Actual pay depends on skills, experience, and education.
Insulet Corporation (NASDAQ: PODD), headquartered in Massachusetts, is an innovative medical device company dedicated to simplifying life for people with diabetes and other conditions through its Omnipod product platform. The Omnipod Insulin Management System provides a unique alternative to traditional insulin delivery methods. With its simple, wearable design, the tubeless disposable Pod provides up to three days of non-stop insulin delivery, without the need to see or handle a needle. Insulet’s flagship innovation, the Omnipod 5 Automated Insulin Delivery System, integrates with a continuous glucose monitor to manage blood sugar with no multiple daily injections, zero fingersticks, and can be controlled by a compatible personal smartphone in the U.S. or by the Omnipod 5 Controller. Insulet also leverages the unique design of its Pod by tailoring its Omnipod technology platform for the delivery of non-insulin subcutaneous drugs across other therapeutic areas. For more information, please visit insulet.com and omnipod.com.
We are looking for highly motivated, performance-driven individuals to be a part of our expanding team. We do this by hiring amazing people guided by shared values who exceed customer expectations. Our continued success depends on it!

Job Description
The Role:
As a 2027 Summer Intern – IndyCar Trackside Engineering, you will support Chevrolet’s IndyCar competition program through data-driven vehicle-performance analysis, engineering preparation, and technical problem solving. Working from the Charlotte Technical Center, you will help convert vehicle, simulation, and race-event data into clear engineering insights and recommendations for the trackside engineering organization. This position does not require travel.
The Team:
The IndyCar Trackside Engineering group supports Chevrolet teams and internal engineering partners by preparing performance analyses, engineering tools, and technical recommendations for competition. The team works across vehicle performance, data analysis, race engineering, powertrain, strategy, and partner-team interfaces to identify performance opportunities and help deliver reliable, competitive race cars. The intern will contribute to trackside engineering activities from the Charlotte Technical Center and collaborate with experienced motorsports professionals.
What You’ll Do:
• Analyze vehicle-performance, telemetry, simulation, and historical race data to identify trends, performance gaps, and opportunities for improvement.
• Support preparation of pre-event analyses, engineering reports, setup comparisons, and post-event summaries for the IndyCar program.
• Develop and maintain analysis tools, dashboards, and repeatable workflows using appropriate engineering and data-analysis methods.
• Assist with investigations involving vehicle dynamics, tire performance, fuel efficiency, race strategy, reliability, and other competition-relevant topics.
• Organize technical information and communicate findings clearly through concise presentations, written reports, and engineering reviews.
• Collaborate with race engineers, vehicle-performance engineers, powertrain partners, and internal GM engineering teams while maintaining data quality and confidentiality.
• Contribute to a safety-focused, disciplined, and continuous-improvement-oriented motorsports environment.
Required Qualifications:
• Pursuit of a Bachelor’s degree in:
mechanical engineering, automotive engineering, aerospace engineering, electrical engineering, computer engineering, data science, applied mathematics, physics, or a related field.
• Must be graduating between December 2027 and June 2029.
• Able to work full-time, 40 hours per week during the summer months.
• Able to work onsite on a full-time basis at the Charlotte Technical Center.
• Strong analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and communication skills.
Preferred Qualifications:
• Experience with vehicle-performance analysis, motorsports, automotive engineering, or another high-performance engineering environment.
• Experience using Excel, Python, MATLAB, or similar tools to analyze and visualize engineering data.
• Coursework or project experience in vehicle dynamics, data acquisition, controls, powertrain, simulation, or race engineering.
• Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative, detail-oriented environment.
• Hands-on experience with engineering projects, laboratory testing, or technical data collection.

VEHICLE
DRAGON
: The Dragon spacecraft is capable of carrying up to 7 passengers to and from Earth orbit, and beyond. It is the only spacecraft currently flying that is capable of returning significant amounts of cargo to Earth and is the first private spacecraft to take humans to the space station.
FALCON
: The Falcon program tackles space exploration’s toughest problems through the ongoing development of our reusable launch vehicles, Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy. These vehicles are currently responsible for delivering commercial, national security, and NASA satellites into orbit, as well as supply critical science, supplies, and crew to the International Space Station.
STARSHIP:
The Starship spacecraft and Super Heavy rocket – collectively referred to as Starship – represent a fully reusable transportation system designed to carry both crew and cargo to Earth orbit, the Moon, Mars and beyond. posting.title: 2027 Summer Intern - Research and Development - Computational Materials Science: Continuum Scales and Materials Discovery
posting.description:
Job Description
The Role:
As a valued Intern in the Mechanics, Materials, and Process Research Lab at General Motors Research and Development, you will advance computational materials science at continuum length scales to accelerate the discovery, design, and deployment of materials for next-generation vehicle and manufacturing applications. You will propose new research directions, establish technical research plans, and lead collaborative studies that connect material composition, microstructure, processing, performance, and engineering requirements.
You will develop and apply continuum-scale models, simulation workflows, and data-driven methods to generate new insights into materials behavior across relevant spatial and temporal scales. Your work will guide experimental research, enable efficient materials down-selection, and help translate computational discoveries into practical materials and manufacturing solutions. You will document and communicate results through high-quality technical reports, external publications, presentations, software or workflow documentation, and records of invention.
The Team:
This position supports the development of advanced materials and manufacturing technologies for future GM products and processes. The intern will work at the intersection of continuum-scale simulation, materials discovery, experimental validation, and application-focused engineering.
What You’ll Do:
Plan and execute collaborative research in computational materials science, with emphasis on continuum-scale materials behavior and materials discovery.
Develop physics-based models for composition–process–structure–property relationships, including constitutive behavior, phase evolution, transport, damage, fracture, fatigue, thermal response, and multiphysics phenomena as appropriate.
Build and apply continuum and mesoscale simulation methods such as finite-element, phase-field, crystal-plasticity, computational fluid dynamics, reaction–diffusion, cellular automata, or related approaches.
Integrate thermodynamics, kinetics, mechanics, processing science, and materials data into predictive computational workflows.
Use simulation, high-throughput computation, optimization, and data-driven methods to screen candidate materials, compositions, processing conditions, and architectures.
Partner closely with experimental researchers to define informative experiments, interpret results, quantify uncertainty, and accelerate materials down-selection.
Establish model verification, validation, calibration, uncertainty quantification, and sensitivity-analysis practices appropriate for research and engineering use.
Connect computational materials insights to manufacturing processes and vehicle-relevant performance requirements.
Drive internal and external collaborations with GM engineering teams, universities, national laboratories, software developers, and research partners.
Maintain awareness of the state of the art in continuum mechanics, computational materials science, materials informatics, scientific machine learning, and related disciplines.
Prepare timely, high-quality technical reports, presentations, publications, software documentation, and invention disclosures.
Generate intellectual property to protect new inventions, computational methods, and research results.
Assist and mentor other employees in accomplishing project and research goals.
Required Qualifications:
Pursuit of an Advanced degree (M.S. or Ph.D.) in one of the following areas: Materials Science and Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computational Science, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Chemistry, or a closely related field.
Must be a current student
Strong foundation in materials thermodynamics, kinetics, mechanics, transport, numerical methods, and structure–property relationships.
Experience developing or applying continuum-scale models to materials, manufacturing processes, or engineering systems.
Experience with one or more of the following: finite-element analysis, phase-field modeling, crystal plasticity, constitutive modeling, damage and fracture, multiphysics simulation, reaction–diffusion, or process simulation.
Experience connecting material chemistry, microstructure, processing history, and performance through computational models.
Proficiency in scientific programming and data analysis using tools such as Python, C/C++, Fortran, MATLAB, Julia, or similar languages.
Experience with numerical algorithms, high-performance computing, version-controlled software, and reproducible computational workflows.
Ability to formulate research questions, translate physical assumptions into models, and communicate model limitations clearly.
Experience working in multidisciplinary research teams.
Strong written and verbal communication skills to work effectively with GM internal and external collaborators.
Able to work fulltime, 40 hours per week during the summer months
Preferred Qualifications:
Ph.D. strongly preferred.
Experience with one or more of the following:
Integrated Computational Materials Engineering (ICME) and materials process–structure–property modeling.
Materials discovery, high-throughput screening, combinatorial design, optimization, Bayesian methods, or active learning.
Phase-field, crystal-plasticity, mesoscale, finite-element, multiphysics, or reduced-order modeling.
Computational thermodynamics, CALPHAD, kinetics, phase transformation, precipitation, solidification, or microstructure evolution.
Scientific machine learning, surrogate modeling, uncertainty quantification, sensitivity analysis, or inverse problems.
Digital twins, process–structure–performance linkages, or integration of simulation with manufacturing data.
Parallel computing, GPU acceleration, cloud or cluster computing, and scalable simulation workflows.
Scientific software development, open-source contributions, workflow automation, or user-defined solver development.
Experience coupling continuum-scale predictions with experimental validation and characterization data.
Demonstrated publication record and/or intellectual property generation.
Experience transitioning computational materials insights into applied engineering or manufacturing solutions.
Experience communicating technical results to both specialist research audiences and product-development or manufacturing teams.
GM does not provide immigration-related sponsorship for this role. Do not apply for this role if you will need GM immigration sponsorship now or in the future. This includes direct company sponsorship, entry of GM as the immigration employer of record on a government form, and any work authorization requiring a written submission or other immigration support from the company (e.g., H1-B, OPT, STEM OPT, CPT, TN, J-1, etc).
The position is subject to export control restrictions and requires the successful candidate to be a U.S. Person (U.S. citizen, U.S. permanent resident, asylee or refugee).

Company:
At Boeing, we are all innovators on a mission to connect, protect, explore and inspire. From the seabed to outer space, you’ll learn and grow, contributing to work that shapes the world. Find your future with us.
Join our exclusive
Graduate Researcher Program (GRP)
in Engineering & Technology Innovation (E&TI) during the Summer of 2027 and you can build something better for yourself, for our customers and for the world.  E&TI is Boeing's global research and development team developing and implementing innovative technologies that make the impossible possible and enabling the future of aerospace. We are engineers and technicians, skilled scientists and bold innovators. Join us and put your passion, determination, and skill to work building the future! #TheFutureIsBuiltHere #ChangeTheWorld
What is Graduate Researcher Program?
The GRP (Graduate Researcher Program) is a unique 10-12 week internship program designed specifically for students pursuing their PhD. GRP is a hybrid experience of real-world industry work experience combined with development programming that exposes students to Boeing, its products, services and its people.  GRP focuses on deeply connecting students to their team and Boeing through work experience across multiple summers with the goal of ultimately offering a full-time position at the conclusion of academic studies if a mutual fit is achieved.
How GRP Works
:
GRP host teams post intern requisitions aligned with Boeing’s strategic needs, aiming to match their needs with top PhD talent. Once candidates apply and are selected, they receive an offer to spend the following summer working with their host team. The program is designed to give interns meaningful, hands-on experience at Boeing, allowing them to apply their academic expertise while contributing to real-world industry challenges and opportunities.
In addition to industry work exposure, students attend GRP programming to further broaden their experience and knowledge of Boeing.  GRP programming components include:  mentorship in your field of study, weekly
Featured Speaker Talks

Innovation Challenge

cannot

completed their
first year of study
in their PhD program by July 2027 and are passionate about the aerospace industry and Boeing. The Aerosciences Group is looking for an Aerodynamics Engineering intern to join the team in Huntington Beach, California. This team develops and applies advanced aerodynamic analysis tools and processes to a wide variety of flight platforms across the flight regime ranging from low-speed/high-lift to hypersonic flight. The products and services of this group cover the complete product life cycle of Boeing's commercial and military aircraft and advanced vehicle concepts.

Development of aerodynamic analysis and optimization tools and processes with the goal of increasing fidelity while reducing cycle time and cost.
Work with CFD developer partners in our team based out of Seattle and St Louis, to develop CFD prediction capability for laminar-turbulent transition.
This position is expected to be 100% onsite.  The selected candidate will be required to work onsite at one of the listed location options.

Background in scientific programming and code development (C, FORTRAN, and/or C++)
Preferred Qualifications:

A strong fluid dynamics background is desired in compressible flows and turbulence modeling

posting.title: Cybersecurity Internship - Spring 2027
posting.description:
About Varda
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.
About This Role
Spring internships will range between the months of January and May.
All dates
dependent upon the university schedule of the selected students. Internships are full-time and on-site in El Segundo, CA. To be considered for this internship, candidates must be actively enrolled in an accredited undergraduate or graduate degree program.
We are hiring a spring cybersecurity intern to help our Information security team with day to day work. You will help us watch for security alerts, write things down clearly, and gather the paperwork we need for our upcoming cybersecurity certification.
This is a real job, not busywork. You will look at real alerts, write real reports, and help us get ready for a real audit. You will sit with our Cybersecurity Analyst and our InfoSec Engineer, and you will learn how a security team works inside a company.
Responsibilities
Help review security alerts that come in each day. You will read them, decide what they are, and write down what you did about them.
Help set up, fine tune, and improve the way our security tools are configured. These tools include Zscaler, CrowdStrike, ThreatLocker, Darktrace, and AlienVault. You will work with your lead to adjust settings, clean up noisy alerts, and make sure each tool is doing its job well.
Help keep our security event logs up to date, so we have a clear record of what happened and how it was handled.
Pull sample logs from our security tools and organize them, so we can show an auditor that we are watching the right things.
Help keep track of the reports we get from our outside security partner, making sure they arrive on time and get filed in the right place.
Help upload reports and updates into the software we use to track our compliance work.
Work on one bigger summer project that you own from start to finish. You will pick this with your lead in the first week. Some examples: a report on gaps in our logging, a refreshed incident response guide, or a simple dashboard.
What You Will Learn
How a information security team runs its day to day work when the company has to pass a security audit.
How the things we do every day (looking at alerts, writing things down, storing logs) turn into the proof an auditor wants to see.
Hands on use of real security tools that protect computers, networks, web traffic, software, and user accounts. You will get real practice setting up and improving tools like Zscaler, CrowdStrike, ThreatLocker, Darktrace, and AlienVault.
How to write clearly about technical problems so that people who are not technical can still understand you.
How the different people on a information security team work together: the InfoSec Head, the analyst, the engineer, the compliance manager, and our outside security partners.
What We Are Looking For
You are a current undergrad in cybersecurity, computer science, information technology, information systems, or a similar major.
You have taken classes or taught yourself at least two of these: networking, how operating systems work, how user accounts and passwords are managed, how to respond to security incidents, or how to watch for security problems.
You are comfortable reading logs and working with data in a spreadsheet. You know what a basic script is, even if you have not written many.
You write clearly. You will be writing notes and reports that other people rely on.
You are organized, you pay attention to details, and you are willing to ask questions when something is unclear.
You are allowed to work in the United States for the full length of the internship without needing us to sponsor a visa.
Nice to Have (Not Required)
You are working toward a beginner certification like CompTIA Security Plus or Network Plus.
You have played with security tools on your own, in a home lab, in a school club, or in a capture the flag competition.
You have used or read about any of these tools: Zscaler, CrowdStrike, ThreatLocker, Darktrace, AlienVault, Okta, or Vanta.
You have heard of compliance frameworks like NIST 800 171, NIST 800 53, ISO 27001, or CMMC and understand the basics.
You can write simple scripts in Python, PowerShell, or Bash.

GE Vernova is looking for a motivated Sourcing Intern to support sourcing, procurement, supplier engagement, analytics, and process improvement activities. This internship is designed for college Freshmen, Sophomores, and Juniors who are interested in building early career experience in supply chain, sourcing, operations, business analytics, engineering, or related fields while contributing to meaningful work in the energy industry.
Job Description
The Sourcing Intern will work with GE Vernova sourcing professionals to learn how supplier relationships, data, compliance, and operational execution support business priorities. The role provides exposure to real-world sourcing processes, cross-functional collaboration, and tools used to support supplier performance, cost productivity, delivery, quality, cash, and continuous improvement outcomes. Interns will receive guidance from assignment leaders and team members while developing professional skills through hands-on assignments, team engagement, and learning opportunities.

Support sourcing projects related to supplier management, data analysis, process improvement, sustainability, and operational execution.
Assist with supplier research, spend analysis, purchase order review, savings tracking, and sourcing performance reporting.

Collaborate with Sourcing, Finance, Engineering, Manufacturing, Materials, Quality, Legal, and other business partners as needed.

posting.title: Mechanical Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
posting.description:
Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military.
With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization.
Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA.
Mechanical Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university.
As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on
complex
projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis.
If you have already graduated from a four-year university, please apply to be an Associate Engineer.
Role
Work together with the engineering team to design, build, and test satellite hardware and/or software.
Design, evaluate, procure, assemble, and test structure, bracketry, and mechanisms for Astranis spacecraft. Components include composite and metallic parts and assemblies with a variety of manufacturing techniques.
Perform mechanical and thermal analysis for spacecraft systems
Integrate parts and systems into the spacecraft by working together with the rest of the team, and document and develop procedures to improve the build process in the future
Requirements
Currently pursuing a B.S. in mechanical, aerospace, or equivalent technical degree (e.g. physics or applied math)
A passion and enthusiasm for hardware development, including working in a fast-paced environment and hands-on design and development
Demonstrated ability to personally design, build, and test hardware from scratch
Don't meet them all? Not a problem, please apply even if you do not meet all these criteria
Bonus
Experience with CAD
Experience with analytical software such as stress or thermal analysis
Experience with electromechanical system design and specification
Experience with control system modeling and design
The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour.

posting.description:
Bloom Energy summer internships are 10-12 weeks and are fully on-site at the office location listed in each job posting. Positions are based in San Jose/Fremont, California or Newark, Delaware.
Individual internships will be posted starting in fall 2026 through spring 2027. Students can apply to this role and can be sourced from it but should apply to specific roles as they are posted if they are interested and qualified.

At Bloom Energy, our vision for a world powered by clean, reliable, and affordable energy is more than just a dream—we’re making it a reality.
For over two decades, we’ve been at the forefront of the global energy transition, pioneering solutions that empower critical industries to thrive in a rapidly digitizing, energy-intensive world. From revolutionizing power for AI-driven data centers to ensuring resilience for hospitals, electric grids, manufacturing facilities, and utilities, our solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) and solid oxide electrolyzer (SOEC) technologies are redefining what’s possible by delivering energy abundance for all. With more than 30,000 fuel cell modules deployed worldwide, we are the trusted partner for Fortune 100 companies and innovators alike. Our cutting-edge solutions enable unparalleled “time-to-power” capabilities, reliability, and sustainability, ensuring our customers remain ahead in a world where soaring energy demand and intensifying energy scarcity are rapidly becoming the new norm.
At Bloom, we thrive on collaboration, bold thinking, and relentless innovation. We believe that, together, we can create a brighter, more sustainable future while tackling the most pressing challenges of the 21st century.

Job Summary:
As a Summer Intern – Methods and Process Engineering at GE Vernova, you will have the opportunity to gain hands-on experience in a world-class manufacturing environment while working alongside experienced engineers and operations leaders.
You will support the development, optimization, and standardization of manufacturing processes for circuit breakers and instrument transformers. Through projects on the shop floor, data analysis, process improvement, and collaboration with cross-functional teams, you will learn how engineering principles and Lean methodologies are applied to improve safety, quality, delivery, and productivity.

They will work to help define system designs, interfaces, and architectures for Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (HVAC) embedded controllers, user interfaces, tools, and digital offerings. In addition, they will help communicate technical direction to senior management and functional teams that span all engineering disciplines, as well as product management, sales, quality, supply chain, and operations.

Support teams on process discipline for new product development.

Work with overall technical leadership on new product development projects.
Participate in the product development life cycle of requirements analysis, design, implementation, integration, and test.

Evaluate trade-offs between possible solution approaches.
Perform system analysis and interface definition.

posting.title: Systems Engineering Intern Summer 2027
posting.description:
ABOUT ROCKET LAB
Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us.
As a Systems Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Pasadena, California, you will have the opportunity to support hands-on integration and testing which includes setting up test hardware, operating robotic systems, executing test procedures, collecting and analyzing data, troubleshooting issues, documenting results, and helping prepare verification and customer deliverable This Systems Engineering team supports the development, integration, and verification of robotic and motion-control systems for active customer programs.
WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO
As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally
Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges
Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates
Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events
YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS
Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results.
Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in a Computer Engineering, Mechatronics Engineering, Robotic Engineering, or related discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship
GPA of 3.0 or above
3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable)
THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE
GPA of 3.5 or above
6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable)
Experience with robotics, motion control, electromechanical systems, or embedded systems
MATLAB, ROS 2, and LabView experience
Python experience
ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS
Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May and June 2027
COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS
Pay Rate: $28.00 USD Hourly
You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs
Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience.
Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match.
Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts.
Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion.

$28
—

WHAT TO EXPECT
We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. Are you ready to explore the world of aerospace and defense? Do you want to learn from and collaborate with some of the greatest minds in the industry? At RTX, our internships, co-ops and full-time careers provide an exceptional foundation to work on complex problems, advance your skills and create a safer, more connected world. Discover opportunities to make a difference at RTX.
What You Will Do
The Electro-Optical System Design Department is currently in need for an Electro Optical Systems Engineer Intern to support the Advanced Products & Solutions Mission Area in the development and building of advanced electro-optical systems.  The systems engineer intern will be part of a design team building electro-optical systems including imagers, passive/active EO tracking, LIDAR, and directed energy systems.  The systems engineer intern will be contributing to assessing systems architecture, developing requirements for these systems, and supporting the design and build efforts.  It will involve being able to assess mission/system requirements and derive design and performance requirements for subsystem and unit levels.  The role also involves understanding verification and test activities to assist in the creation of a proper IV&V plan meeting the requirements of the program.
The EOSD Department supports Space and Airborne Systems (SAS) by providing systems engineering expertise in the Electro-Optical Systems (EOS) domain. Typical roles within the department involve:
EOS System Architects and System Design Engineers
Integrated Product Team Leadership, Lead Systems Engineers, Chief Engineers
Requirements Engineers
EO Systems Analysts
Qualifications You Must Have
Must be pursuing Bachelor’s or Advanced degree in Physics, Optical, Science, Technology, Engineering, or Mathematics (STEM) and actively enrolled through the completion of the internship/co-op session.
Must have a minimum of 30 hours of credit by the start of the internship / co-op session.
Experience with electro-optical infrared imagery, focal plane technology, lenses, or apertures
Experience with fundamental optical principles including geometrical optics, physical optics, imaging systems, aberrations, or detectors
Hands‑on experience through coursework or lab work with optical testing or alignment
Experience may be obtained through job experience, research, coursework, or projects
Qualifications We Prefer
Internship or project experience related to opto-mechanical engineering, photonics, infrared physics, or optical systems
Experience with programming using C++ or Python
Experience or coursework in signal processing, image processing, tracking, computer vision, or machine learning
Knowledge of systems engineering architecture and design, integration and test, and verification and validation approaches

Available for a 6 month project

posting.description:
About Varda
Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules.
Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.
From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.
Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.
Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.
Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

Spring internships will range between the months of January and May.
